chunks: Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from someone who informed him, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them.

Regarding witnesses: if they testify against a man and then retract their testimony, and judgment has already been passed against the man, they are held liable for what they testified to and are made to pay compensation. But if judgment has not been passed, their testimony is discarded and the witnesses are not charged anything.

key_terms.الشُّهُودِ: the witnesses giving testimony in a legal case
key_terms.رَجَعُوا: they retracted or withdrew their testimony
key_terms.ضُمِّنُوا: they were held liable for the consequences
key_terms.غُرِّمُوا: they were required to pay compensation or a fine
key_terms.قُضِيَ: a judgment was issued or decided

ai.seo_question: What happens in Islamic law if witnesses retract their testimony after judgment has been passed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about witnesses who retract their testimony after testifying against a man. If a judgment has already been issued on the basis of their testimony, they bear financial liability; otherwise, their testimony is simply rejected without penalty.
